blocking_focus: Complete the candidate-bound Tester MCP state matrix.

preservation_constraints.requirement: Keep frozen technical baseline `native_godot_project` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

Keep frozen technical baseline `host_godot_boot` passing. Do not treat this as a mandate to preserve the same visible asset, map, HUD family, or material choice if a higher-quality replacement is available and the PRD still fits.

task_specification.objective: Repair the authored arena integration, complete the ordinary five-wave and Bellkeeper lifecycle with truthful upgrade presentation, and make the dense native-renderer profile deterministic and recapturable while preserving the authored world and host/native baselines.

diagnosis.root_cause: Release convergence is blocked by three distinct surfaces: the ordinary five-wave/Bellkeeper route is not proven end to end, the authored arena still has landmark visibility and collision/framing drift during traversal, and dense-profile qualification lacks a native-renderer recapture path because the bound environment is llvmpipe.

stop_conditions: Do not replace, split, hide, or surgically alter the preserved authored cemetery package.
Do not treat instrumentation or llvmpipe measurements as native qualification; Tester and GameLoop Runtime own recapture and verdicts.
Stop after the bounded candidate repairs and required same-loop retest evidence are available for the three phase gaps.

strategy.rationale: Use three materially different root-cause families: rebase gameplay datum and sight-lane isolation against the intact authored map, repair authoritative wave/lifecycle transactions and upgrade presentation, and complete renderer-gated dense profiling instrumentation for later native-host qualification.

code: Run import/boot and native project integrity checks after implementation.
Check authoritative wave, boss, result, Retry, pause/reset, upgrade transaction, spatial collision/navigation, and dense-profile state contracts for runtime errors and duplicate terminal events.
Verify development-only tester/profile actions remain unavailable in release exports.
runtime: Tester/GameLoop Runtime recaptures spawn, critical-route, cardinal landmark, ordinary movement/dash, five-wave progression, Bellkeeper phases, victory/result, Retry, upgrade focus across keyboard/mouse/gamepad, and dense prepare/advance/reset states.
Run direct black-box plus white-box retests for arena collision/occlusion and ordinary route completion; verify reset isolation, no stale entities, no duplicate rewards, and no skipped waves.
Run three isolated dense cycles at 1920x1080, record renderer classification and distributions, and leave native qualification explicitly pending/rejected when hardware eligibility is absent.
visual: Capture shipped high-angle gameplay at spawn, critical route, central building/landmarks, perimeter, dash, dense combat, Bellkeeper, Result, Retry, and level-up choice states.

Confirm larger traversable scale, external depth, readable landmark silhouettes, collision-aligned streets and perimeter, no disappearance/occlusion drift, readable wave/boss HUD, and authored choice icon/stat hierarchy.
Use adjacent state/time frames only for dash, boss transition, level-up, Result, and Retry changes; recapture failed cells first and stop after bounded retest.

done_when: Expand the playable space to a larger traversable scale while retaining coherent external world/external depth around the intact authored package.
The central building and every required landmark remain readable from spawn, critical route, and cardinal/perimeter views; no disappearance or camera occlusion drift occurs during traversal or dash.

Collision and navigation agree with visible streets, structures, and the boundary/perimeter; ordinary movement and movement replay cannot pass through landmarks, hit invisible barriers, or leave the arena.
Spawn, objective, and camera framing are rebased to native authored streets without proxy-floor takeover, and the shipped high-angle camera keeps the player, threats, and an escape lane visible.
tasks.instructions: Repair the arena integration around the preserved authored cemetery scene using a root-cause strategy different from prior camera transform tuning. Inspect the authored package transform, outer datum, navigation, collision bodies, spawn lanes, objective anchors, and ArenaCamera sightline logic. Rebase gameplay coordinates and isolate only the minimum additive collision/navigation/sight-lane supports; keep one intact authored environment instance and minimize unrelated proxy/support geometry. Provide direct black-box movement/dash replay and white-box spatial/collision receipts for Tester recapture.
tasks.title: Rebase authored arena scale, collision, and landmark visibility

done_when: A fresh ordinary run advances through five authored waves in order with visible progression, escalating composition, safe spawn behavior, and no skipped or duplicated transitions.

The Bellkeeper transition, two-phase boss encounter, defeat, victory/result presentation, and clean Retry/reset are reachable through ordinary authoritative gameplay; pause/resume does not corrupt wave or boss state.
Automatic combat, enemy damage/death/drop, XP pickup, level-up transaction, selected upgrade, and visibly changed weapon behavior remain causally connected in the ordinary route.

Level-up choices replace text-stacked cards with authored visual hierarchy: weapon/upgrade silhouettes, compact stat icons, truthful current-to-new values for no more than three decision-relevant stat deltas, no NEW or LOCKED placeholder in CURRENT values, no unchanged or exhaustive rows, restrained copy, and complete keyboard, mouse, and gamepad focus states.

Tester can directly retest the route and lifecycle through black-box input plus white-box wave, boss, result, retry, and upgrade snapshots, with no stale entities, duplicate rewards, or one-shot terminal callbacks after reset.
tasks.instructions: Complete the ordinary five-wave director/Bellkeeper route in the existing authoritative systems. Trace and repair wave timing, spawn budgets/caps, enemy motion and damage, XP/upgrade transactions, boss transition, victory/result, pause, and Retry/reset guards rather than adding synthetic route shortcuts. In the same bounded family, finish the upgrade draft presentation and focus behavior to satisfy the required choice hierarchy. Add only candidate-owned diagnostics needed to expose current wave, boss phase, terminal, reset, and choice predicates; keep development-only controls unavailable in release exports.
tasks.title: Complete ordinary five-wave, Bellkeeper, retry, and upgrade-choice flow

done_when: A deterministic dense-profile prepare/advance/reset path runs the representative 25–40 enemy scenario using normal authoritative spawning, combat, pooling, UI, VFX, lights, and audio without changing ordinary release tuning.

Each cycle records renderer identity and hardware eligibility, target 1920x1080 viewport, frame/physics/render distributions, active entities, pool reuse/exhaustion, lifecycle deltas, and runtime error counts with requested/resolved/reset-isolation receipts.
Three isolated cycles are reproducible and aggregate under one contract; software/llvmpipe sessions are explicitly surfaced as rejected or pending rather than misclassified as native qualification.

The dense path produces no unbounded allocations, orphan/stale entities, pool exhaustion, recurring runtime errors, or release-export exposure, and preserves host_godot_boot and native_godot_project baselines.
tasks.instructions: Complete the candidate-owned dense profiling path needed for later native-host qualification. Inspect the existing DenseWaveProfile and RunController sampling lifecycle, renderer preflight ordering, deterministic enemy workload, pooling, and reset isolation. Repair missing guards, metric fields, cycle aggregation, or release-build gating so Tester can perform three identical native 1920x1080 prepare/advance/reset cycles. Do not tune ordinary wave balance or claim native performance from the current llvmpipe environment; retain explicit renderer status and sample availability for host review.
